title: Gradle Lifecycle and the Task DAG

scout.purpose: Turn gradle lifecycle and the task dag into a predictable, testable build-system contract.
scout.realWorldUse: Large Android builds must produce trustworthy variants quickly across developer machines and CI while tooling and module graphs evolve.
scout.outcome: Model the build behaviour, implement it with lazy public APIs, and verify correctness plus performance.

blocks.text: Gradle initialization evaluates settings, discovers projects and included builds, and establishes plugin and dependency-management context. Configuration evaluates participating project build logic, registers tasks and model values, and constructs the requested directed acyclic task graph. Execution schedules only tasks in that graph, subject to dependencies and constraints. This explains why top-level println calls run even for help, while code inside a task action runs only when the task is selected. Diagnose phase mistakes before adding flags or memory.

blocks.text: The task graph models required work, not chronological script order. dependsOn adds a prerequisite; mustRunAfter changes ordering only when both tasks are present; finalizedBy schedules cleanup even after failure; shouldRunAfter is a preference. Prefer dependencies inferred by connecting a producer output Provider to a consumer input, because data flow and execution order stay consistent. A cycle means the work model is contradictory. Use dry runs, task reports and build scans to inspect the selected graph rather than guessing from console order.

blocks.caption: A focused build fragment; its full correctness depends on declared inputs, lifecycle, compatibility and functional evidence.

blocks.text: Configuration must describe work cheaply and without performing it. Network calls, source scanning, dependency resolution, environment mutation and file generation during configuration slow every invocation and undermine configuration caching. Put repeatable work in typed task actions with declared inputs and outputs. Treat settings, plugins, projects, configurations and tasks as different model layers with defined ownership. A build is maintainable when a developer can predict which phase owns each effect and why a requested task selects its dependencies.

Build logic is production infrastructure: it shapes every developer feedback loop and release artifact. Make ownership, inputs, outputs, compatibility, security boundaries, failure messages, metrics and rollback explicit. Prefer public typed APIs, lazy Provider wiring and deterministic isolated tasks. Verify the model through representative local and CI workflows, clean and incremental changes, parallel execution, relocated workspaces, configuration-cache reuse and trusted build-cache restoration. Measure before optimising, then preserve correctness with functional tests and regression budgets. Avoid hidden environment state, internal APIs, task-name guessing, global project mutation, mutable network inputs and credentials in logs or reusable outputs. Record the supported Gradle, AGP, Kotlin, Java and operating-system matrix, and make upgrades controlled experiments with safe rollback evidence. A fast build is valuable only when it produces the right traceable artifact consistently.

blocks.title: Common build trap
blocks.text: Watch carefully for this common failure mode in production: Calling an expensive function while configuring a registered task still performs that work during configuration; placing text inside the registration block does not make it an execution action.

trap_check.mistake: Calling an expensive function while configuring a registered task still performs that work during configuration; placing text inside the registration block does not make it an execution action.
trap_check.why: The build may become eager, stale, nondeterministic, incorrectly variant-aware or unsafe under parallel and cached execution.
trap_check.fix: Use the public model, declare the complete data flow and add a functional regression test.

trap_check.mistake: Optimising a synthetic clean build without measuring the team’s frequent workflow.
trap_check.why: The change can shift cost or complexity without improving developer or CI feedback.
trap_check.fix: Baseline representative workflows and compare controlled before/after critical paths.

challenge_intro.task: Trace initialization, configuration and execution for three Gradle commands, draw their task DAGs, and refactor one configuration-time side effect into declared execution work.
challenge_intro.successLooksLike: The build behaviour is correct for clean, incremental, parallel and cached paths and has measured evidence, diagnostics and ownership.

recall.answer: The requested tasks and the directed dependency graph Gradle constructs for that invocation.

recall.prompt: What makes custom Gradle work trustworthy?
recall.answer: Complete declared inputs and outputs, deterministic isolated execution, lazy wiring, public APIs and functional tests.

recall.prompt: What should precede a build-performance change?
recall.answer: A representative workflow, controlled baseline and evidence locating the critical path or avoidable work.
